page: Amazon Web Services t9g.micro is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 dedicated physical cores running at a clock frequency of 3.3 GHz with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is constrained to 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 0.5 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for persistence. Baseline network throughput is listed at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Because of its low resource ceiling, the hardware footprint is geared toward minimal operating system images, background monitoring daemons, microservices, lightweight development environments, and low-traffic edge workers. The arm64 instruction set provides strong energy and compute efficiency relative to its entry-level hardware class, though memory-bound workloads or applications requiring substantial local disk IOPS will experience bottlenecks without external EBS optimization and careful footprint management.
description: Amazon Web Services t9g.micro is an entry-level burstable instance powered by 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton processors on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz, matching 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. System memory is sized at 1.0 GB, yielding a 0.5 GB per core allocation. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and the instance includes no hardware GPU acceleration along with a 0 Gbps baseline network profile. Designed for highly resource-efficient operation within the lowest compute tier, the t9g.micro provides a cost-effective platform for lightweight development servers, low-traffic microservices, administrative jump boxes, and basic containerized services with minimal memory overhead.
